items.title: Signal is blocking screenshots to prevent Gemini and Siri AI from scanning your chats
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Signal is introducing protections to prevent Gemini and Siri AI from scanning private conversations on Android and iOS 27. 
 The protections also block users from taking screenshots inside Signal, but they can be disabled. 
 Signal is calling on Google, Apple, and Microsoft to give app developers better tools to restrict AI access without compromising app functionality. 

AI assistants are increasingly doing things on our phones that would previously require us to open an app ourselves. Gemini can already order food and book rides using third-party Android apps , and just yesterday, Google started rolling out similar computer-use capabilities on Macs . Meanwhile, Apple’s Siri AI can understand what’s on your iPhone’s screen. But what happens when the app an AI assistant tries to read contains information that was never meant to leave it?

That’s a question Signal is tackling head-on. The encrypted messaging service announced today that it is introducing protections against AI assistants capturing its content on Android and iOS 27.
items.t: Signal is blocking screenshots to prevent Gemini and Siri AI from scanning your chats

items.title: One UI 9.5 code hints Samsung will push its own updates to its Android laptops
items.summary:
Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 shows Samsung’s Setup Wizard on its upcoming Android laptops will ask you to agree to automatic software updates from Samsung. 
 Samsung’s Software update and Device Care apps also have laptop versions, with RAM Plus virtual memory and McAfee scans, but no Maintenance mode. 
 On Googlebooks from other brands, Google rolls out software updates itself, so Samsung’s approach could mean its laptops won’t follow the standard Googlebook update model. 

Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops aren’t just shaping up to work like a Galaxy phone with a keyboard, but they could also get updated like one. We’ve already covered the laptops codenamed Origin , their dedicated One UI interface with Circle to Search , how they’ll plug into the Galaxy ecosystem , the on-device Galaxy AI features for their Snapdragon X Elite chip , and features like Camera continuity, texting, and app streaming from your phone . Digging further into the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on my Galaxy S26 Ultra, I found that Samsung is also building its own software update and device maintenance apps into these laptops.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

How Samsung will update its upcoming Android laptops is notable because on Googlebooks from other brands, Google rolls out Googlebook OS updates itself , not the laptop maker, and promises up to 10 years of updates .
items.t: One UI 9.5 code hints Samsung will push its own updates to its Android laptops

items.title: Gboard is testing a new paste shortcut that keeps your formatting intact
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Gboard is working on a new toolbar shortcut that lets users paste text while retaining original formatting, including bold, italics, and others. 
 This toolbar option appears to be limited to the most recently copied text, and won’t apply to other items on the clipboard. 
 Android already offers a way to do this, but requires users to long-press the text field and manually pick an option from the context menu. 

Gboard is comfortably among the best keyboards for Android phones , and it could soon gain an upgraded paste experience for copied text. Right now, Gboard’s toolbar automatically pulls up the clipboard shortcut so you can paste text instantly. However, there’s no option to preserve the original text formatting, with the keyboard defaulting to plain text. It now looks like Gboard is working on changing this in a future update.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We dug into version 18.8.0.10 beta of Gboard to activate an additional toolbar shortcut alongside the existing one, with first-time users seeing an introduction message that reads “Paste while preserving all formatting.”
items.t: Gboard is testing a new paste shortcut that keeps your formatting intact

Google is replacing the traditional Google Search button with new Gemini-related controls.

Google wants to make AI Mode more easily accessible to users, which is why it’s now rolling out a new set of visual changes to the iconic homepage on the web. This includes dedicated buttons for three new Gemini-powered features and a sidebar to access your recent AI Mode searches and queries.

Robby Stein, VP of Product for Google Search, recently posted on X about the new Google homepage that is now rolling out globally. Meanwhile, the new interface also has an unfortunate casualty: the traditional Google Search button, which is being phased out.
items.t: Google’s homepage is losing its iconic ‘Google Search’ button in favor of Gemini

items.title: Samsung’s Android laptops will grab photos and scans straight from your Galaxy phone
items.summary:

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 shows Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops will likely support Camera continuity, letting you insert a photo, scanned text, or table rows and columns from your Galaxy phone into a document on the laptop. 
 The laptops will also call and text using your phone’s number, and could stream apps from your phone. 
 Currently, Samsung’s Windows Galaxy Books handle these features through separate Windows apps, while Google’s Googlebooks already offer their own takes on calling, texting, and phone app streaming. 

Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops are shaping up to work a lot like a Galaxy phone with a keyboard. We’ve already covered the laptops codenamed Origin , their dedicated One UI interface with Circle to Search , how they’ll plug into the Galaxy ecosystem , and the on-device Galaxy AI features for their Snapdragon X Elite chip . Digging further into the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on my Galaxy S26 Ultra, I found that Samsung is also building Camera continuity, texting, and app streaming into these laptops.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Many of these features already exist on Samsung’s Windows-based Galaxy Book laptops, but they live in separate Windows apps there. Googlebooks from other brands also have Google’s own versions of some of them. On the Origin laptops, Samsung appears to be building its own versions into One UI itself.
items.t: Samsung’s Android laptops will grab photos and scans straight from your Galaxy phone

items.title: Gboard beta rolls out new clipboard setting that lets you keep copied items for up to 24 hours
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is rolling out a new clipboard history setting in Gboard beta. 
 Users can choose how long copied items remain in the clipboard, ranging from the default one hour to 24 hours. 
 Pinned clipboard items will continue to be stored indefinitely, regardless of the selected duration. 

One frustration with the Gboard clipboard is that you can copy something, get busy with other tasks, and come back to find it gone. That’s because Google’s keyboard automatically clears copied items after an hour unless you pin them. Google is now giving users more control over how long those items stick around.

Back in August, we discovered that Google was working on customizable clipboard history in Gboard . Three months later, the feature is starting to roll out to beta users.  Android Authority ‘s AssembleDebug, who originally spotted the feature in development, has now received the new clipboard setting in Gboard version 18.8.0 beta.
items.t: Gboard beta rolls out new clipboard setting that lets you keep copied items for up to 24 hours

items.title: Samsung’s Auto Blocker won’t switch off during calls in One UI 9.5
items.summary:
Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

With One UI 9.5, users won’t be able to change Auto Blocker settings during a call. 
 This is to thwart scammers trying to get people to disable security features. 
 The feature is already live in the first One UI 9.5 beta on the Galaxy S26. 

Samsung’s One UI comes with Auto Blocker , which warns you before sideloading APKs and protects your Galaxy phone or tablet from malicious execution over USB or from harmful files received via messaging apps. With One UI 9.5 beta that rolled out to the Galaxy S26 series earlier this week, Auto Blocker appears to be getting additional anti-scam features that prevent hackers from misguiding users during calls.

Since Auto Blocker prevents unauthorized apps from being installed, scammers may often attempt to lure users into changing security settings on their devices. Getting users to change these settings makes it easier for scammers to install malicious apps and take over these devices. To prevent this, Samsung is raising the threshold for Auto Blocker and adding measures that prevent users from changing crucial settings while they’re on calls.
items.t: Samsung’s Auto Blocker won’t switch off during calls in One UI 9.5

items.title: Samsung could bring native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama to its smartphones with One UI 9.5
items.summary:
Samsung announced the One UI 9.5 beta program for the Galaxy S26 series yesterday. One UI 9.5 brings several new features, including App Lock and Floating shortcuts. With future One UI 9.5 updates, Samsung could bring more features to Galaxy smartphones, including native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama.

This revelation comes from Android Authority, which found strings related to native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama in One UI 9.5's Camera app code.

Open Gate uses the entire imaging area of the camera sensor instead of cropping it to a 4:3 or 16:9 aspect...
